stances.claim: Trump is the 'MOST SUIT-able PRESIDENTIAL ASPIRANT' in storied US history -- never has any presidential aspirant been as legally and politically vilified, yet he leads GOP polls and edges Biden in the general election.

The Colorado Supreme Court's 4-3 ban under 14th Amendment Section 3 is, as CJ expected in his Sept 4, 2023 column, the natural legal consequence of the Capitol attack -- and the Maine Secretary of State has done the same; the question is whether Scotus will uphold either.

Trump's five-argument defense (the prohibition doesn't cover presidential candidates, no insurrection, no Trump role, free-speech protection, conviction-first requirement, and functus officio limitation) ranges from technically arguable to flatly implausible -- but Scotus will decide.

Trump's 'presidential immunity' defense in the four pending criminal cases would put him 'beyond the reach of the rule of law' -- 'Tell that to the marines!' -- and how Scotus rules, given that six of nine justices are GOP-appointed (three by Trump himself), will reveal how independent Scotus really is.

The character assessment Tony Lopez quoted from the NYT -- wielding power carelessly and cruelly, encouraging violence and lawlessness, exploiting fear and hate, undermining the rule of law, applauding dictators, plotting retribution -- and Nikki Haley's tighter 'Chaos follows him' together capture Trump as utterly unfit for high office.

notable_anecdotes: The 'MOST SUIT-able PRESIDENTIAL ASPIRANT' wordplay -- punning on the lawsuits Trump has accumulated -- used as the column's most memorable single coinage, capitalized for emphasis.

The five-argument catalog of Trump's 14th-Amendment defense -- including the functus-officio argument that the post-Civil-War provision has accomplished its limited purpose -- laid out without endorsement to let readers assess each.

Trump as 'the only former US president to be arrested, detained (later released upon posting a $200,000 bail), and taken scowling mug shots of' -- the precise documentation that gives the column its 'most-vilified' factual foundation.
'Tell that to the marines!' -- CJ's idiomatic exasperation at the presidential-immunity defense; a rare colloquial American idiom for him.

Trump's public expectation that 'the six conservative justices, especially the three he appointed' will side with him 'no matter what' -- quoted as the most damaging Trump utterance against Scotus independence.

Tony Lopez's NYT-quoted character indictment -- wielding power carelessly and cruelly, encouraging violence, exploiting fear, applauding dictators, plotting retribution -- the longest third-party quotation in CJ's recent US-politics columns.

Nikki Haley's 'Chaos follows him' -- CJ's selection of this as 'the short, apt, and memorable description' over the NYT paragraph, demonstrating CJ's appreciation for epigrammatic political characterization.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban catalogues Donald Trump's unique status as the 'MOST SUIT-able PRESIDENTIAL ASPIRANT' -- never in storied US history has any aspirant been as legally and politically vilified, yet he overwhelmingly leads the GOP nomination and edges incumbent Joe Biden in general-election polls. CJ focuses on two sets of legal threats. First, as he expected in his Sept 4, 2023 column 'Prosecuting and disqualifying Trump,' the Supreme Court of Colorado (4-3) and the Maine Secretary of State have banned Trump from their respective GOP nomination processes under Section 3 of the 14th Amendment, which bars from public office any person who 'engaged in insurrection or rebellion against the [US], or given aid or comfort to [its] enemies.' Trump's appeal to Scotus argues five defenses: the prohibition covers 'person' and 'public office' but not 'candidates for president'; the Jan 6, 2021 Capitol attack was not insurrection; Trump had no role in it; his verbal outbursts were First-Amendment-protected; the ban requires a prior criminal conviction; and the amendment is functus officio because its Confederacy-targeting purpose has been accomplished. Second, four criminal cases in Georgia, New York, Florida, and Washington DC could incarcerate Trump for life -- he is the only former US president to be arrested, detained (released on $200,000 bail), and 'scowling' mug-shotted, with many co-defendants having plea-bargained. His 'presidential immunity' defense would put him 'beyond the reach of the rule of law' -- 'Tell that to the marines!' How Scotus rules, given that six of nine justices are GOP-appointed (three by Trump himself) and Trump has publicly expected them to side with him 'no matter what,' will test the Court's real independence. Tony Lopez of the Manila Overseas Press Club quoted The New York Times calling Trump 'utterly unfit for high office... wielding power carelessly and cruelly... encouraging violence and lawlessness, exploiting fear and hate for political gain, undermining the rule of law and the Constitution, applauding dictators... plotting retribution.' But former South Carolina governor Nikki Haley said it shorter: 'Chaos follows him.' CJ's solution: the GOP should sober up and nominate the rising, brilliant, young 51-year-old Haley instead of the demagogic, self-indulgent, unpresidential, authoritarian 77-year-old Trump -- and Haley can, IMHO, easily trump the forgetful, frail, 81-year-old Joe Biden.
